english: they were obstinate they disobeyed. The Jews murdered the Lord through their own ill will, not so that they might fulfill the prophecies; for if it were so they would have been irreligious in that way.

God did not harden them, but allowed them to do what they wished. And they had the hardening from unbelief. Yet it was impossible that God’s foreknowledge, which foresaw the unbelief, not come out—not as compelling. Those unable to believe do not have a nature opposing belief, but a bad choice. Therefore the devil darkens them and God does not hinder.
For this reason the prophets foretell, so that the sober may flee the devil’s pits; for “they could not” stands in place of “they would not”; and elsewhere too we understand power as choice.

God did not harden their heart; for if he had, he would not have required of them an account, since he even forgives voluntary faults, but hands over the obstinate, blinded by the devil, to passions and a “depraved mind” (Romans 1:28); for while they were such, it was not just that they know the depth of the mystery—those who had shut the eyes of their mind.

Being image of the Father he shows the Father through himself. Through this he signifies the indistinguishability of essence, showing the consubstantial; for the divine is incorporeal. These things signify likeness.
Because of the hearers’ weakness he speaks as man. When I am honored, do not think you honor a man; for through me the Father is honored.

As the Father is light, so also the Son. Therefore Paul, wanting to show the great resemblance, calls the Son “radiance” of the Father (Hebrews 1:3): just as light appearing makes both itself clear and the things seen, so the Son, being light and having come, made both himself and the Father known to us.
The aim of the present coming was not to judge but to save the faithful. And so as not to give them occasion for unbelief, he refers the cause of unbelief toward him up to the Father.

For the word of his humility condemns them. The Son himself is going to judge the disobedient, not the word; for he speaks enigmatically. On the day of judgment the word that called us to salvation punishes those who disobeyed.

Being Word of the Father he himself interprets what is in the Father and makes it manifest. Therefore he also says he has received a commandment; for so among us too word publishes what is in the mind.
He says he does these things as from the Father, since the Jews saw him reshaping the shadow of the law toward the more spiritual.
Saying this he did not abolish his own authority, but shows that nothing alien to the Father is in the Son. I utter nothing contrary to the Father, nor as mine alone, but as common.

He foreknew the passion; therefore it must be said that he came willingly to suffer; for he would not unwillingly have endured so insulting a death. He calls hour the Passover feast at which he suffered; he calls his death a passing.

He loved them even before the Passover, having become man; but when he also handed himself over to die, then he perfectly showed his love toward human beings. Not only Jews but also others he has as his own as Creator. He calls his own all who are in the world.
He calls tradition the salvation of the faithful, which he himself also hands over in turn to the Father, because he was begotten from the Father’s essence.

As astonished the evangelist says that he washed the feet of the one who had set himself to hand him over to death. On the fifth day the supper; on the fourth Judas agreed to betray Christ; therefore he said the devil had already cast into the heart that Judas should betray him.
Through the touch he was cleansing their feet for readiness of the gospel. And he also leads them into humility.
When I am taken up, he says, then from the Spirit’s grace you will learn what is happening.

Having at first spoken against it through humility, now through excess of reverence Peter says something superfluous—both from fierce love.

They were clean, enlightened by the teaching and freed from Jewish error and having cast off all wickedness by being with Christ. And by witnessing purity to the others he proves unclean the one who is not clean.
By saying “I am” he showed that he is God by nature and teacher.
Not because they were filthy did he wash them, but to teach them to be moderate. The basin does not hold the rank of a bath nor lighten sins, but leads toward perfect virtue.
Not only in word but also in deed he gave the example of perfect humility.

It is not knowing virtue that is to be emulated, but working it; for knowing and not doing brings greater punishment. Knowing happens to belong to many; doing does not belong to all. Therefore he said: blessed are you if you do them.

Judas was not compelled to betray so that the Spirit’s words might come out—which is full of every blasphemy—but so that we may know that Scripture spoke about that one whom we see having done what was foretold. And if the Lord chose Judas and he transgressed, nothing follows from this; for he chose him while he was good, and he was changed like Adam and Saul; for God does not abolish free will, but allows each to act as he wishes, so that the wicked may be punished and the virtuous crowned.
Through the morsel the Lord fulfilled the prophecy that says: “He who eats my bread has lifted up his heel against me” (Psalm 41:9; John 13:18).

On the fourth day Satan cast into Judas that he should betray the Lord, and he spoke this to the Jews on the fifth toward evening. When he saw Judas wanting to betray the Lord in deed and hurrying to it, then he entered into him. So casting in is one thing and entering into him another, just as striking someone with the hand from outside is one thing and giving him an opening and thrusting the sword in is another.

The evangelist calls the devil’s entrance the confirming of Judas to do what is pleasing to the devil. When God made him plain and set him apart, then the devil sprang upon him because of his measureless shamelessness.

He does not say this as commanding, but as reproaching the one he let do what he wished, since he did not want to be corrected. Since this is settled for you, hasten to the plot against me; for suffering does not grieve me.
The morsel given him in the order of a blessing was not the cause of Judas’s apostasy, but the unchangeable wickedness after the exposure. Therefore the enemy also sprang in as into an ungated city.

Since perhaps John said it to him secretly and he heard, no one knew; for if they had known, perhaps they would even have killed him—or because they were in turmoil, not knowing what was in Judas’s heart, they did not understand what was said.
If someone says how the one fed from others’ means, who did not allow the disciples to carry a bag or purse, had a money-box, it must be said that this happened only for the sake of the poor.
Even if the Son does all things, yet through what he does he ascribes them to the Father and glorifies the Father.
Christ, as having put death to death through his own death, was glorified; he teaches that enduring what is shameful for God’s sake is glory.
The Father was glorified in the Son, since it became known whose Father he is. So also the Son is glorified as having such a begetter.

Through himself the Father will glorify the Son, and at once—that is, on the cross, when the sun was darkened, the rocks were split, and after fifty days the Spirit descending made the Son plain to all.
They were seeking him as one who loves and as a teacher.

New is the form of this commandment, and beyond the law is loving the neighbor more than oneself. I do not want you to love those to whom you owe, but those to whom you do not owe; for I too die for you, to whom I owe nothing.
Not from the signs you do will you be known as my disciples—for that belongs wholly to grace from above—but from loving one another and having concord and giving yourselves.
Christ is a son of love, who is love according to nature, being love itself by nature and fruit of love, not having the good of love as something acquired.
Because of weakness he forbids Peter to follow him, yet later promises because of boldness. Since he too was going to be crucified as Christ was, he foretells what will happen to him alone.
Peter has become a type for us of asking teachers what we do not know.
Disbelieving somewhat what was said, Peter inquires, and so also promises to die for him.

Since you do not want to be persuaded that what I say cannot fail to happen, you will know it in the denial. And he underwent this not because Christ led him into it, but because he left him bare, so that he might not be lifted into arrogance.

Let no one say that Peter denied because Christ said so; for he did not lay necessity on him so that he should come to denial, but as God he foretells to the disciple what was altogether going to be. And the denial did not come from an unbelieving soul, but from weakness.
Not all of you are going to deny, he says; Peter’s denial will be wiped out through repentance and confession.
If the place in which you are going to be with me had not long ago been prepared for you, I would have gone away and prepared a place for you.

There is no need to ascend for the sake of preparing a place for you, but so that I may make you a pasture of ascent where the angels’ dwelling is, which was impassable to all flesh. When therefore I do this, coming “in the regeneration” (Matthew 19:28) I take you with myself, that you may be where I am.

He is way because through him they were coming and he himself was Lord of leading up to the Father. Truth because of truthfulness, that these things will altogether be. And life, because not even death itself, he says, will be able to hinder you from coming.
He is way through the practical, truth as true definition of the faith, life as raising us and leading into incorruption and freeing from the ancient curse.

Here he calls sight the knowledge according to mind. Therefore the one who contemplates the Son not in bare essence but clothed in flesh knows his equal Father in all things. Knowledge shows contemplation through notions; vision shows assurance through God-befitting works.
As knowing the Son exactly he said this, thinking perhaps he could see God with the eyes.

Nothing else, he says, is the Son except what the Father is while remaining Son; for even if you happen to say, Philip, that I know you, that you are Son, yet you have not recognized me, that having the whole Father in myself I remain again being Son.
From what the Son has done both before incarnation and after incarnation, his infinite strength appears to the mind as “in a mirror” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

The wording signifies the extreme resemblance and equality. Therefore, lest someone fall into Sabellius’s heresy by dividing the hypostases, he adds saying: the one who has seen me has seen the Father. And this he makes clear through knowledge. He says these things about the invisible essence of himself and of the Father; for it is not possible to see the divine with fleshly eyes. Therefore he said: the one who has seen me has seen the Father—not that he himself is the Father, but that through the extreme resemblance the one who sees the Son sees the Father; for each is self-subsistent.

An earnest of the coming life, which you are to receive, is my resurrection. He says the disciples live not only the present life but the coming one.

Under fear and grief they were beside themselves and silent.
Unless I suffer, the Spirit who is cause of every good gift does not come upon you.

So great is the power of the Holy Spirit’s descent that then the sin of those who have offended against me will be made plain. As many as after the Holy Spirit’s descent did not believe in Christ remained in their own sins; the one who did not believe in the sinless one is condemned as a sinner.

He was condemned as having killed through the Jews the Christ who is sinless, since he was making excuses saying that Adam did not die through me but because he sinned. And since after the passion healings happen through the Holy Spirit, through the deeds the devil’s overthrow is shown.

Unjust is the one who did not believe in the righteous one taken up into the heavens for his righteousness and become unseen to human beings. Slack, because though Satan was crushed he still would not conquer him.

english: That is: he speaks in agreement with me; for the Spirit is not lacking; being self-subsistent as consubstantial with Father and Son he knows all things and has power of himself to act.

When the Spirit teaches you, then you will be able to leave the legal types and make the worship “in spirit and truth” (John 4:23–24). The Spirit is not greater than the Son, he says. Therefore he will speak nothing from himself, but what he hears; for what I say, that one also will say. The Spirit will teach human beings the things of the Son’s Godhead and glory and of equality with the Father. He does not fail to speak from weakness; he said this because of the exact harmony of the Trinity.
As the Son naturally has the Father’s things through the consubstantial, he said that the Spirit’s own things are also his, as the things of the Trinity are common.
So as not to grieve the disciples, he also did not say “I die,” but “you do not see me.”
Under grief they did not understand, and that he was departing they knew, but how he would come they did not know; for they were ignorant of the resurrection before the outcome.
Since being deeply grieved they did not want to hear about his death, wanting to fix this doctrine in them he said “you will weep”; after the grief there will be joy.

The reward of your grief will be joy, as also for the woman in labor the joy from childbirth after the grief. Since when he died it appeared to them to pass from grief into joy, he used the example of the woman giving birth.
Since you will be persuaded that as God I rose and die no longer, even if with the flesh I go up into heaven.
He means the time of the resurrection.

For as in proverbs Christ speaks these things as one going on to say; for it cannot be understood according to the letter. And that one asks and receives who asks what is profitable for bettering souls. He calls proverb the unclear and veiled word. Because of their infancy he speaks in a shaded way. But when you advance, then I unveil to you the Father’s glory. After the resurrection I will speak clearly to you the things about the Father. When you receive the Spirit, then you will receive clear knowledge about Son and Father.
He can as God give, yet as already saying “I ask” he stayed with the word by economy as man.

From the essence, he says, I came out from the Father, being indivisibly in the Father and having the Father self-subsistently in myself. Neither when he became man, left behind by the Father, is he said to have come into the world, nor when he was taken up with the flesh was he left behind by the world; for he is God filling all things.
The “now you believe” he says more humanly; for insofar as I am God, I am in God and Father naturally and without interval. He said this by condescension, since the disciples wanted to hear this.

Christ appeared better and more powerful than every worldly sin and also gives the faithful to conquer. Or that Christ, having come to be from us insofar as man, appeared better than death and corruption and the grace passes over to us. And so we ought to take courage that we will receive, since as man he conquered and we seem in him to have conquered; for if as God he conquered, it is nothing toward us.
He calls hour the fitting time of the passion, at which he judged to suffer—as also he said about the wine—not the hypostasis-less fate.
Through the form of prayer he trains us in trials to pray and take refuge in God.
So that the hearers may not take offense, by economy he says “what you have given me.”
It must be noted that right faith is the true life that grants its own goods to those who believe. He says he was sent not as from necessity serving the Father’s will

He is said to glorify the Father having done all things unto incarnation, or that the Father’s power is made known through his Son, if he speaks as man; for through what the saints accomplish, God is glorified.
Nothing is the Father’s that is not the Son’s and the reverse. Through my equality with you I am glorified by everyone.
By economy as man he speaks of God’s name having been given him, having it by nature as God and Son.

He did not drag them by necessity. Therefore Judas also perished through voluntary obstinacy; not only Judas but many others also perished, not with Christ; for as far as it lay with him, no one perished. He was called son of perdition as awaiting like a birth the day of perdition.

According to idiom Scripture sets as a cause things that happen from the outcome. Judas, having learned what was foretold, ought not to have betrayed Christ. And if someone says how he perished while Christ was keeping them, it must be said that he does not keep the base but lets them free to do what they wish, yet keeps and empowers the good because human choice is not enough to keep a person.
He says these things so they may not lose heart but rather rejoice that he goes to the Father.

When he says they are “from the world,” he means nature. When he says they are not, he says it because of guilelessness, as he also was. And the “as” here is not of exact indistinguishability. What he says is this: they have become heaven-citizens and have nothing in common with the earth; for the difference of natures is great, that he is God by nature and they are human beings.

Since the disciples were going to do something like what Christ did, he says they need sanctification through the Spirit, so that they may be able to run through the inhabited world unhindered by the evil one.

Not only for the disciples but also for all the faithful Christ asks that the grace given through the Holy Spirit be given—the grace that reshapes the human being into the divine image. And this union does not happen according to essence or according to hypostasis, but according to the agreement of faith, by which the faithful knew that the Son was incarnate by the Father’s good pleasure; for this is being sent.

All sacrifices are called holy as brought to God. And he said “in truth” because sanctification through the sheep was in type—or that I also dedicate them to you as an offering—or that when the head was sacrificed this happened—or that they also presented “their bodies” as a “living sacrifice” (Romans 12:1)—or also that without death he made them a sacrifice by being slaughtered for them.
When they are counted worthy of the unity spoken of, then they know that you sent me.

He calls glory that of signs and doctrines and like-mindedness. Being himself the giver, because of the hearers he shapes the request. And as man he is said to receive what belongs to him by nature; and he means the Spirit’s grace.

Through what he says—the one who gave and the one who received—he shows the hypostases of Father and Son. And again by saying he himself was before the world he refutes the heretics who say that from Mary’s times Christ had his beginning, as having the glory before the world. He said before the foundation of the world; for “you have given me” is of condescension. And he did not say that they may share his glory, but that they may behold it, which is the faithful’s greatest rest and glory.
To persuade the disciples that he came willingly to the passion, he went away to a place known to Judas, so that he might not escape notice and did not shut himself in as in a prison.

english: spoke everything calmly, and neither from the voice did Judas or the rest recognize him, except when he wished.
Because of the disciples’ weaknesses he puts them outside trials as God; he always keeps the disciples, only letting Judas perish by preferential wickedness.

As wanting to die for the teacher he did this. Peter, taking courage from what Jesus did, himself also did this. And let no one accuse Peter as a murderer, since he did this not defending himself but the teacher; yet they were still incomplete. Through the type he shows that the Jews will be empty of every right hearing.
Binding him they fulfilled Isaiah’s word: “Let us bind the righteous” (Isaiah 3:10 LXX sense). The Lord was bound so that he might free us from devilish bonds.
John went in with Jesus among the crowd unrecognized, and then as known he spoke to the doorkeeper and brought Peter in.

He asked what he taught his own disciples, asked him whether he agrees with what is through Moses or introduces another teaching and what his disciples are persuaded of, so that if he finds him opposing Moses’ things he may hand them also over to the Jews as God-fighters.

He exposes him pretending not to know things spoken in the open. And if he taught all things openly, the secret things said about him by some are not acceptable. Ask the servants who earlier marveled at the teaching and now are arresting me.

And without being ordered the servant struck Christ, since Christ himself hinted saying “see, these know”—those who once heard and praised—and wanting to free himself from the suspicion that he was among those not marveling, he himself did this; for he would not have spoken something fitting so as to be moved from this to strike him. He exposes the servant wronging him not only because he simply struck him, but because having earlier marveled he now without finding fault dishonored him.
When the evil one shook Peter he was defeated of his promise.
They did not kill him themselves as being under Romans, so that they might not be punished by Pilate.

Honoring the type they did not enter—that is, a sheep; for they were going to sacrifice the Passover according to the law that had no force among them. Or he calls Passover the whole feast, or that it was preparation day, when also the old Passover happened.

Without cause they declared that he had justly been handed over; they call a reasonable cause their arresting him, as if they err in doing nothing unjust. If your law also punishes the guiltless, judge him yourselves. Clear proof that the Lord suffered willingly: from what, knowing, he foretold that he was going to be handed over to the nations to be crucified.

As having fallen from rule—for they were under Romans—they said this. Or it is not permitted to crucify him; for so they wished, that they might also parade the manner of his end. Or that he calls himself king and the charge is public and it belongs to you to put him to death.
He says these things wanting to free him.
The angels were quiet while their king was insulted, understanding the economy of Christ’s presence.
He looses Pilate’s anxiety persuading that he is not a rebel but king of heaven and earth. Therefore Pilate is without defense, not as killing him as a blasphemer but as a favor to the Jews.
For this I became man and was born from Mary, that driving falsehood and the devil from the world I may show the divine nature reigning over all.

Even if you are a ruler, yet finding no fault against me you could not condemn me, unless I willingly by the Father’s good pleasure led myself to suffer.
For in that very feast they killed him.

The evangelist marked the hour because of the resurrection that happened on the third day. The fine scribe, instead of the gamma letter which signifies the third, wrote the marked sign which the Alexandrians call Gabex, which shows the sixth, having much likeness to each other. And through the scribal error the disagreement happened; for instead of third hour he wrote sixth.

Through being crucified in the midst of two robbers the Scripture was fulfilled that says “and he was numbered with the lawless” (Isaiah 53:12). These are a type of the two peoples who are condemned through their sins—or that those who cling to Christ ought to crucify themselves as dying to the former way of life, yet living in newness according to the gospel.

Not finding what to say against him Pilate wrote this, so that he too might not be thought a robber. He publicly proclaimed him king and that the Jews killed their king, writing to mock the Jews. This is “the handwriting” which the sentence against Adam nailed to the cross, which the devil holding led all human beings into death as none wholly doing what seems good to God—and dying for us on the wood he freed us.
The Jews’ impiety reached its end, and he willingly endured the death according to the flesh and bowed the head because the flesh’s tones were dissolving.

He bowed the head; for it was not nailed, and then he expired; for he was Lord of all, though custom has first expiring and then bowing the head. The Jews’ impiety reached its end, and he willingly endured the death according to the flesh and bowed the head because the flesh’s tones had been dissolved. The end shows the separation of the soul from the body.
They pretend to honor the day and ask a favor so that the men may die more quickly. They ask so that another Scripture may again be fulfilled that says a bone of him will not be crushed.
One of the soldiers, disbelieving whether he had died, pierced his side.
The blood shows redemption and the water sanctification. Through water the church is born again and through blood and flesh she is fed.

The evangelist confirms that he himself is the Christ proclaimed beforehand through the Scriptures; for the deeds came out in agreement with what was said about him. Bone is understood as the taut and unbreakable of the mystical word. And since the sheep bore the image of the Lamb of God, one is fed the head of Christ by taking the things about his theology, the feet by being taught the things about his incarnate economy, and the inwards the hidden doctrines; for each of the doctrines about Christ has a hidden and mystical word. Since therefore bone is understood as the taut of the mystery, those who fittingly and harmoniously hold the mystery about Christ—a bone of him will not be crushed. When he comes to judge, then they will see him and mourn.

english: Arimathea, a stranger. And if he had been with others, some of the unbelievers were going to say that it was not Jesus’ body that rose but another’s. He was laid in a new tomb because of the strangeness of the run back from death into life and the novelty devised against corruption. It was arranged that the place be near, so that the story about theft might also be shown false.

Though Matthew said the resurrection happened in deep evening, and John early while it was still dark, they do not disagree about the time of the resurrection, but ran together into the same time of hours; for one moves from the end and the other from the beginning into the very middle of the night.
Christ rose while the stone still lay and the seals. And the tomb is opened toward faith in the signs that happened. Unclear is the time of the resurrection as also that of the second coming.

What those trying to show them disagreeing want, I do not find; for if about the resurrection they had not brought out the same judgment, or had not said the same day on which the resurrection happened to occur, or had not all alike reported the women first come for honor of the dead, they would have some pardon for this absurd and foolish censure; but if in the things aforesaid they showed much agreement—alike announcing the resurrection, saying the day is the same, the women alike come—what ever does their exactness about the hours want? I at least do not understand, and yet I think nothing else so tends to establish the truth of what was said as that those who showed much agreement in the most crucial things are found disagreeing in some very small things and in what it was likely that being human they would err, showing the exchange of words by brief hours; for if wanting to lie they had chosen an agreeing judgment about this, nothing would have hindered. Having once chosen to lie about this, keeping much and exact agreement in all, it lay before them to lie and each by himself would fulfill his own aim. Necessity surely was that they vary a little, many things being what forced them to suffer these things.

And if Luke says that the disciples disbelieved those about Joanna, nothing contrary; for they had not yet gone away to the tomb and did not believe as it happened, as going to bear witness as eyewitnesses to the resurrection. Or they disbelieved those about Joanna as having heard from the two men, but were persuaded by Mary saying that they took the body.

This is not contrary to Luke also that Peter alone went away to the tomb; for when after seeing the linen cloths he went away, later those about Joanna came saying that the Lord rose, and Peter alone ran again to the tomb hoping perhaps himself also to see some vision.

This was a mark of the resurrection; for if enemies stole it, they would not have left the garments for profit, and if they were friends they would not have endured to insult the body naked; for if the disciples had seized it, they fled because of the guarding soldiers and Jews and would not have stood stripping the body and setting the cloths apart and the napkin apart. And it shows that a body that has passed into incorruption has no further need of garments. They did not see him risen, but from the gathering of the garments they conceive the resurrection and believe this, holy Scripture crying it. When the angel appeared, the guards fled terrified and therefore those around Peter came to the tomb without fear.
They understood and believed the word of the resurrection which earlier they did not know. Before the experience the disciples did not know the word about resurrection.

english: The disciples also fled to themselves by God’s economy, so that they might not suffer something before the proclamation, but Mary, conceiving nothing perfect, remained weeping at the tomb not only because he had died but also because she thought the Lord’s body had been moved.

So that she might weep more, she stooped into the tomb, to whom the angels speaking guidingly say “why do you weep,” urging her to ask something and learn about the resurrection, for which also they appeared clothed in white.
Remaining through affection she was counted worthy also of the angels’ vision.

To those he appeared more wondrous, but to the woman in a humble form, so as not to frighten her. Therefore she also thought him to be a gardener. She sees the Lord and did not recognize him either because of the darkness or because by God-befitting power he covered himself. By economy she turned and saw the Lord yet did not recognize, so that she might not be troubled as seeing a demonic fantasy; for she still suspected that he was dead.
Swallowed by grief she still doubted about the resurrection.
With a certain manner the Lord names her, so that even so she may come to perception that he both rose and was present.

Since as far as it concerns you I am not God but a mere man about to be again with human beings according to the way of life before the passion and you do not think I will be with the Father, do not touch me.
As more intimate he grants this one the boast of the good news, as returning more than the others at the tomb and going about the tomb.
Since according to the essence of flesh the Son became our brother, as God by nature existing as the Father’s Son he says his Father; and God, as man according to us, he names God his God.

Since entering with the doors shut he made the disciples doubt whether perhaps what appeared was not a body but only a type, Luke clarifying the mind said: “Handle me and see, that a spirit does not have flesh and bones” (Luke 24:39) and he ate and showed the flesh’s wounds.

Through this he showed the Godhead’s strength. He did not present himself by day, so that all might be gathered; on the day he spoke with Mary he also appeared to the disciples by God-befitting power and with the doors shut, wondrously and unexpectedly appearing to them; for he was God, even if he had the thick body.

He showed the marks of the passion so that they might be assured that it was the same that had suffered, even if it had become spiritual and they had passed into incorruption. For this he showed them, to put all their turmoil to sleep.

Through this the word was fulfilled which the Lord said: “a little and you will see me,” “and your heart will rejoice” (John 16:16–22). Through the word of peace he looses their cowardice. “He himself is” Christ “our peace” (Ephesians 2:14). Yet through this we also were taught in the mystical assemblies to say to ourselves the word of peace.
Since through the cross all things have become easy, I send you to do the work which I did.

He gave them a spiritual gift of loosing sins and condemning. And others say that he made them fit for reception of the Spirit which they were going to receive after the ascent. Through what he breathed and gave spirit, he showed that it is consubstantial with him and not alien and proceeding through him from the Father, which nerved them to do what is pleasing to God and to know the power of the mystery according to God. And the breathing made the renewal for humanity and taking again the “according to the image” which Adam had before the transgression. And saying he sends, he sent ahead of time to confirm that this will be for all at the appointed time.
And Thomas, though absent, obtained the Spirit’s grace through the breathing; for upon the whole choir of the apostles the Lord poured out the grace.

Beyond measure Thomas, busying himself through thinking it impossible, is charged. Therefore he did not say only “unless I see,” but “unless I handle,” lest what is seen be a phantom. Hearing then from the disciples that he took a lance wound, he was persuaded even without seeing, but as beyond reason he disbelieved the resurrection. He said it not so much as disbelieving as grieving that he too was not counted worthy of the sight. And by economy Thomas disbelieved, so that through him we all may know that the crucified body rose; for by seeking to see the wounds about the flesh, he was seeking whether that very flesh rose.
For the shock of the signs almost draws even the unwilling who see toward faith.

He shows himself having wounds and allows him to handle him; for by condescension he so appeared to Thomas though freed of every thickness of body and become light, so that he might be persuaded that it was the same crucified body. And from using Thomas’s words he shows that even when Thomas was saying these things he was present. And even if bodies are raised incorruptible and lacking nothing in the new resurrection, yet so that no word of unbelief may remain, as Thomas sought to see, so he showed; and not only Thomas but also the angels ignorant of the economy of the incarnation and saying: “Who is this who comes from Edom” and again: “What are these wounds in the midst of your hands?” teaching he says: “with which I was struck in the house of my beloved” (Zechariah 13:6).

The whole contemplation of this section is as follows. Those before the disciples passing the time in darkness of demonic error caught nothing or very few, which is in place of nothing; nor those worshipping in types and shadow, where they themselves despising the law obeyed human commandments; but also the throng of the nations was un-netted, not receiving the divine lessons. But when the “sun of righteousness” (Malachi 4:2) came, hungering for humans’ salvation, he found nothing edible among humans and says to cast the evangelical word, which is the right teaching, compared with which the law and the prophets are understood as left; and by the grace of the one who commanded they drew many; for the wonder upon this surpasses the apostles’ strength.

Peter draws the spiritual net with the others, bringing the catch to Christ. And the hundred are understood as the fullness of the nations, the fifty as the race from Israel saved according to election, and the three invent the showing of the holy Trinity, to whose glory the life of the faithful caught is understood conjoined.
“Come, breakfast” has a riddle in the word: that after the toils rest and food and enjoyment will succeed the saints.

english: the first things were of condescension. And he does the human things before the passion. And if Luke said that he also “ate,” not as still needing the flesh but for demonstration of the resurrection.

Wanting to rekindle him from the despondency after the denial he asks him, and through the three questions and confessions he wipes out the three voices of the denial and through words he sets right the faults that happened in words. And from this a custom has come that three confessions be required of those about to be baptized.
He asks him a third time not as not knowing—for how, also the one who foretold his passion?—but to show that he cares greatly for the oversight of his sheep and that Peter loved him greatly.

This signifies the death through the cross, which he underwent unwillingly, even if for the hoped-for things he was put to death willingly. Some from this thought that Peter suffered unwillingly, but it is not so; rather he wanted to suffer, yet did not want to be crucified, lest he seem among the simpler to have been counted worthy of the same honor as the Master. Therefore he teaches him not to be troubled; for this form is not of choice but brought on by others.

He said this wanting to cut off the untimely sympathy they had toward each other; for if they were not separated from each other, the inhabited world would have suffered the greatest loss. And he did not say “he does not die,” but “if I want him to remain”—that is: a work was entrusted to you, do this, care for your own; for what do you want, if I do not wish to send him with you but that he remain here?

The disciples received the Lord’s word as a decision that he will not die, which he did not say. But what he said, speaking in riddle, he said the long-livedness of his life; for in the times he died without punishment.

As having spoken without falsehood he bears witness to himself the truth. Therefore in many places naming himself indefinitely here he plainly signifies himself; for he himself is the one who wrote the gospel. One loved by God would not have been able to lie, therefore do not doubt; for the truth would not have loved him loosening the truth.

One must refuse to speak the things better than all writing in books, which not even the world itself can contain because of the greatness of contemplations. If all were written, no human would suffice for acquiring the books. For this it was not written, so as not to overpass the memory of the hearers. Or if all were written, the books would be numberless and no one could know all. Or if someone wants to present the greatness of what happened, neither the world nor human hearing contains them. Some say that those living worldly cannot contain hearing the God-signs according to what was said in the beginning: “and the world did not know him” (John 1:10), as also the Lord himself said that “not all contain this word” (Matthew 19:11).
Many and numberless are the God-signs and from many these were taken that can perfectly benefit.

So many are the things done and said by the Savior that all libraries would be full, he says I think, of books containing the histories of the Lord’s works and the words upon them, if one were going to write all according to each.

We understand the name of the world differently. And it is possible according to one meaning to present the truthfulness of the word and to refute the rashness of those who mindlessly mock the God-breathed words of the evangelists.
